title: Against war, drought and hunger: A global coalition to prevent a food crisis - European Council on Foreign Relations
gist: Three shocks are converging on global food supply in 2026: Russia-Ukraine strikes have cut Ukraine's exports by 75% and taken over 90% of Russia's grain export capacity offline, the blocked Strait of Hormuz is stopping about a third of global seaborne fertiliser reaching fields, and a possible record El Niño threatens harvests. With food prices already almost 75% above their 1999 lows and 2.2bn people food insecure, ECFR proposes a European-convened coalition with commodity-specific ceasefires and a $500m CGIAR productivity push.

themes.theme: Hard numbers on the supply shock

insights.claim: Global food prices are already almost 75% higher than their 1999 lows and almost 2.2 billion people face food insecurity, before the three incoming shocks land.
insights.so_what: The starting level matters: the shock arrives on top of an already elevated price base, so the tail for further spikes is fatter than in 2022.
insights.quote: Global food prices are already almost 75% higher than their 1999 lows.
insights.speaker: Cary Fowler, Jana Kobzová, Jim O’Brien

insights.claim: Global wheat production is expected to fall 3% in 2026-27, with sharply worse national numbers: 8% in the EU, 12% in Australia and 19% in Argentina.
insights.so_what: Specific country-level wheat supply cuts across three major exporters — the core bullish input for wheat futures and for importing-country inflation.
insights.locator: It may reduce already falling rates of wheat production
insights.speaker: Cary Fowler, Jana Kobzová, Jim O’Brien

insights.claim: Ukraine and Russia together generate 30% of world wheat exports, 20% of corn and 60% of sunflower oil, with Russia alone supplying 20% of global fertiliser — concentration that makes the Black Sea the single most important node in the global food system.
insights.so_what: Quantifies exactly how much of world supply is hostage to one war — the base case for tail risk in soft commodities.
insights.locator: There are two bright spots among the big global agricultural producers
insights.speaker: Cary Fowler, Jana Kobzová, Jim O’Brien

insights.claim: Russian attacks have cut Ukraine's agricultural exports by 75% with more damage in August, while Ukrainian strikes have taken over 90% of Russia's grain export capacity offline — both major Black Sea exporters are now crippled simultaneously.
insights.so_what: The mutual destruction of export infrastructure is the most underappreciated bullish driver for grain prices — it is not a one-sided blockade this time.
insights.locator: Russia’s attacks on Ukraine’s highly exposed grain and port infrastructure
insights.speaker: Cary Fowler, Jana Kobzová, Jim O’Brien

insights.claim: The Strait of Hormuz is the largest single conduit for the nitrogen fertilisers most directly linked to yield and the export route for about half the global supply of sulphur used in phosphate fertilisers, so roughly one third of global seaborne fertiliser cannot reach fields.
insights.so_what: Hormuz is a fertiliser chokepoint, not only an oil one — a mechanism most energy-focused risk models ignore, with direct read-through to nitrogen and phosphate producers outside the region.
insights.locator: Meanwhile the Strait of Hormuz remains blocked
insights.speaker: Cary Fowler, Jana Kobzová, Jim O’Brien

insights.claim: The World Food Programme's conservative pre-El Niño budget needs for 2026 are only 34% met so far.
insights.so_what: The funding gap is the binding constraint on any mitigation, and the number to watch around UNGA pledging.
insights.locator: The World Food Programme’s conservative pre-El Niño budget needs
insights.speaker: Cary Fowler, Jana Kobzová, Jim O’Brien

themes.theme: Second-order effects that persist for years

insights.claim: Rising prices and exhausted government subsidies in states like Malawi are deterring fertiliser use, which depresses future production — a multi-year yield hit that outlasts the initial price shock.
insights.so_what: Fertiliser affordability today sets harvest capacity two to three seasons out, extending the food-price cycle well beyond any ceasefire.
insights.locator: Rising prices and exhausted government subsidies in states like Malawi
insights.speaker: Cary Fowler, Jana Kobzová, Jim O’Brien

insights.claim: El Niño events are historically associated with protectionism — India has already imposed export restrictions hitting south-east Asian countries — which raises prices, lowers margins and curbs investment in future output.
insights.so_what: Export bans are the reflexive policy response and the amplifier that turns a weather shock into a price spiral; watch rice first.
insights.locator: Historically, El Niño events are associated with protectionism
insights.speaker: Cary Fowler, Jana Kobzová, Jim O’Brien

insights.claim: A super El Niño would bring heat and drought to southern Africa, significantly reduce production in south and south-east Asia, and drive up rice prices.
insights.so_what: Names the specific geographies and the specific grain — rice — most exposed to the climate leg of the shock.
insights.locator: A “super El Niño” will likely bring heat and drought
insights.speaker: Cary Fowler, Jana Kobzová, Jim O’Brien

insights.claim: Logistics compound the problem: war damage to infrastructure and low water levels in the Danube make it harder to get grain out of the region even where it is produced.
insights.so_what: Alternative export routes that worked in 2022 are physically constrained now, removing the main pressure valve.
insights.locator: Logistically, war damage to infrastructure and low water levels
insights.speaker: Cary Fowler, Jana Kobzová, Jim O’Brien

insights.claim: In 2022 a UN- and Turkey-facilitated arrangement kept Russian and Ukrainian grain and fertiliser flowing through alternative routes, but in 2026 the UN is approaching a leadership transition, the US has turned against the organisation and there is no global focal point for action.
insights.so_what: The institutional capacity that absorbed the last shock is absent — assume a longer, more disorderly adjustment this time.
insights.locator: In 2022, a UN- and Turkey-facilitated arrangement mitigated a similar crisis
insights.speaker: Cary Fowler, Jana Kobzová, Jim O’Brien

insights.claim: There is a good chance that the two wars driving up food prices, in Ukraine and Iran, will escalate in the near future, and Russia especially would be reluctant to join any commodity ceasefire.
insights.so_what: The author's own base case leans toward escalation, not resolution — a reason to treat food-price relief scenarios as low probability.
insights.speaker: Cary Fowler, Jana Kobzová, Jim O’Brien

themes.theme: The proposed coalition and its price tags

insights.claim: The proposal is a European-convened coalition combining states influential with the combatants — India, China and Turkey especially — with the states most exposed to the nutritional crisis, meeting on the margins of UNGA in the week of September 21st.
insights.so_what: A dated, checkable diplomatic catalyst; whether ministers actually convene is the first test of the thesis.
insights.locator: European leaders, including those of the UK and Ukraine
insights.speaker: Cary Fowler, Jana Kobzová, Jim O’Brien

insights.claim: A CGIAR-led sustainable productivity growth push is proposed with a budget of $500m over three years, front-loaded to support the upcoming planting season.
insights.so_what: A small, specific funding ask relative to the scale of the problem — cheap optionality on yield outcomes in exposed regions.
insights.locator: A CGIAR-led sustainable productivity growth push
insights.speaker: Cary Fowler, Jana Kobzová, Jim O’Brien

insights.claim: Technical assistance works at scale: a CGIAR-led programme reached almost 6m African farmers in 2023-5 and in Malawi delivered maize yields 64% higher than the national average.
insights.so_what: Evidence that drought-resistant seed and soil-fertility programmes produce measurable yield uplift, supporting the case for agricultural-input investment in Africa.
insights.locator: A programme to distribute food relief and technical assistance
insights.speaker: Cary Fowler, Jana Kobzová, Jim O’Brien

insights.claim: The Iran element requires exempting Iran's own fertiliser and urea exports and other fertiliser shipments from the US blockade and securing Iran's wheat and rice imports, overseen by an expert-level group modelled on the 2022 Black Sea arrangement.
insights.so_what: The specific sanctions carve-out that would have to happen for fertiliser flows to resume — a discrete, watchable policy trigger for nitrogen prices.
insights.locator: The programme should also involve an agreement with Iran
insights.speaker: Cary Fowler, Jana Kobzová, Jim O’Brien

insights.claim: A partial Russia-Ukraine ceasefire limited to attacks on grain ships and on ports and infrastructure central to grain, fertilisers and inputs is presented as the achievable ask, rather than a general ceasefire.
insights.so_what: A commodity-scoped ceasefire is the realistic de-escalation format to watch — it would reprice grain without resolving the war.
insights.locator: Coalition members should strive for a partial ceasefire
insights.speaker: Cary Fowler, Jana Kobzová, Jim O’Brien

insights.claim: The middle-power core proposed to carry this includes Brazil, Egypt, Kazakhstan, Mexico and Turkey, with Brazil, India and South Africa able to invoke Russia's claim to speak for developing countries as fellow BRICS members.
insights.so_what: Maps the actual diplomatic coalition that could move Russian and Iranian behaviour — middle powers and BRICS leverage, not the G7.
insights.locator: Along with the UN secretary-general, and a core group of middle powers
insights.speaker: Cary Fowler, Jana Kobzová, Jim O’Brien

insights.claim: The initiative is framed as a “no regrets” effort: even if combatants never join, supporting farmers and global trade improves the food situation and builds momentum toward Black Sea and Hormuz agreements.
insights.so_what: A sequencing logic that lets Europe act without waiting for Russia or Iran — useful for judging whether any announced coalition is substantive or symbolic.
insights.locator: This initiative is intended to be a “no regrets” effort.
insights.speaker: Cary Fowler, Jana Kobzová, Jim O’Brien

source_meta.author: Cary Fowler, Jana Kobzová, Jim O’Brien
